PA-2025-HB2885.title: An Act amending Title 16 (Counties) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in fiscal affairs, further providing for tax levies.
PA-2025-HB2885.aiSummary: Would change Pennsylvania rules for county tax levies, which are the taxes counties can raise to fund their budgets.

PA-2025-SB1403.title: An Act amending Title 35 (Health and Safety) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in emergency medical services system, further providing for receiving facilities and providing for transportation coverage; and abrogating a regulation.

votes.motion: Committee vote (Institutional Sustainability & Innovation): Reported as Committed
Committee vote (Institutional Sustainability & Innovation): Reported as Committed

PA-2025-SB1403.aiSummary: The bill would change rules for ambulance drop-off sites, called receiving facilities, and let the health agency set more types of places that can take patients, including help for people in a behavioral health or substance use crisis. It would also require payment rules for ambulance treatment and transport, so insurers, Medicaid managed care plans, and CHIP managed care plans pay the emergency service amount when a patient is taken to a receiving facility. The act would take effect 180 days after it becomes law.

PA-2025-HB2519.title: An Act amending Title 18 (Crimes and Offenses) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in assault, further providing for the offense of strangulation.
PA-2025-HB2519.aiSummary: The bill would require police to give a verbal or written warning to a person they believe may have been strangled. The warning would explain that strangulation can cause serious injury or death, even without visible signs, and would urge quick medical care. Police would also have to record whether they gave the warning, and the law would take effect 60 days after passage.

PA-2025-SR411.title: A Resolution designating the month of November 2026 as "Good Samaritan Law Awareness Month" in Pennsylvania.
PA-2025-SR411.aiSummary: The resolution would name November 2026 as "Good Samaritan Law Awareness Month" in Pennsylvania. It would also encourage state and local government branches to raise awareness of the state's Good Samaritan laws, which give some protection to people who report a drug overdose.

PA-2025-SR408.title: A Resolution recognizing November 17, 2026, as "Pennsylvania Veterans Day of Caring" in Pennsylvania.
PA-2025-SR408.aiSummary: The Senate resolution would recognize November 17, 2026, as "Pennsylvania Veterans Day of Caring" in Pennsylvania. It would also encourage residents to support veterans through kind acts, community involvement, and ongoing help. The focus is on Pennsylvania veterans and the people who choose to take part.

PA-2025-SR400.title: A Resolution urging the Congress of the United States to establish terms of 18 years of regular active service for justices of the Supreme Court of the United States.
PA-2025-SR400.aiSummary: The resolution would urge Congress to set 18-year active service terms for U.S. Supreme Court justices. It would also call for those terms to be staggered so a vacancy opens every two years, and for justices who finish a term to move to senior status, which means a lighter judicial role. It would ask Pennsylvania's members of Congress to support and advance the change.

PA-2025-HB2706.title: An Act amending the act of March 4, 1971 (P.L.6, No.2), known as the Tax Reform Code of 1971, establishing the Pennsylvania Child and Dependent Care Enhancement Tax Credit Program; and making a repeal.

actions.text: Amended in House Committee on Appropriations

votes.motion: Committee vote (Appropriations): Re-report Bill As Amended
Committee vote (Finance): Report Bill As Committed

PA-2025-HB2706.aiSummary: The bill would create a Pennsylvania tax credit for resident individuals who already claim the federal child and dependent care credit. The credit would apply to work-related care costs, with limits of $3,000 for one qualifying person or $6,000 for two or more, and it could be refunded if the credit is more than the person owes in state tax. It would also repeal an older Fiscal Code section and take effect right away.

PA-2025-HB1345.title: An Act amending the act of June 13, 1967 (P.L.31, No.21), known as the Human Services Code, in public assistance, providing for medical assistance coverage for menopause treatments.

votes.motion: Committee vote (Appropriations): Re-report Bill As Committed
Committee vote (Human Services): Adopt Amendment A04306
Committee vote (Human Services): Report Bill As Amended

PA-2025-HB1345.aiSummary: The bill would make Medical Assistance cover treatments for menopause for eligible people in Pennsylvania. It would include FDA-approved drugs and devices, behavioral therapy, and treatment for menopause caused by a hysterectomy. The state would need federal approval before this coverage starts.

PA-2025-SB381.title: An Act amending Title 35 (Health and Safety) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in public safety, prohibiting certain animal experimentation and certain testing and sale of animal-tested cosmetics; and providing for remedies.

votes.motion: Committee vote (Rules & Executive Nominations): Re-Reported as Committed
Committee vote (Appropriations): Re-report Bill As Committed
Committee vote (Judiciary): Report Bill As Amended

PA-2025-SB381.aiSummary: The law limits the use of state money for certain animal research, including painful studies on dogs and cats and devocalization, which is a surgery to alter an animal’s voice. It also requires some animal testing facilities to offer dogs and cats for adoption before euthanizing them, and it bars the sale of dogs and cats bred by people with certain federal animal-welfare violations. Schools and other recipients of state funds that use animals in research must also share reports on their spending, projects, and animal use.

PA-2025-HB69.title: An Act amending the act of May 13, 2008 (P.L.139, No.14), known as the Cancer Drug Repository Program Act, further providing for title and short title of act, for definitions, for establishment, for restocking and dispensing of cancer drugs, for storage, distribution and fees and for immunity; providing for annual report, for list of approved participating pharmacies and for limitations; further providing for regulations; and imposing duties on the State Board of Pharmacy.

PA-2025-HB69.aiSummary: Pennsylvania Act 61 of 2026 became law and changes the cancer drug repository program into a prescription drug repository program. It lets approved pharmacies accept certain unused prescription drugs and give them to indigent patients if the drugs meet set safety rules. The State Board of Pharmacy must issue rules, post a public list of approved pharmacies, and send an annual report to lawmakers. The act takes effect in 60 days.

PA-2025-HB36.title: An Act amending the act of April 9, 1929 (P.L.177, No.175), known as The Administrative Code of 1929, in Office of State Inspector General, further providing for definitions and for powers, purpose and duties.

votes.motion: Committee vote (State Government): Reported as Committed
Committee vote (Appropriations): Re-report Bill As Committed
Committee vote (Judiciary): Report Bill As Committed

PA-2025-HB36.aiSummary: This law updates the State Inspector General office rules in Pennsylvania. It adds a definition for an "enforcement officer" and lets those officers carry firearms while doing their official work if they follow office rules and finish required firearms training. It took effect right away.

PA-2025-HB2555.title: An Act amending Title 3 (Agriculture) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in domestic animals, further providing for definitions and providing for requirements for equines sold by dealer.

Committee vote (Agriculture & Rural Affairs): Report Bill As Amended

PA-2025-HB2555.aiSummary: Pennsylvania Act 88 of 2026 changes animal law rules for horses and other equines sold by a dealer. It requires a negative equine infectious anemia test, or a health inspection paper, microchip, tattoo, or brand as allowed, and it exempts foals under 6 months old if they are with their mother and she tested negative. Dealers must keep sale and health records for at least two years, and the act takes effect in 90 days.

PA-2025-HB1972.aiSummary: The law changes the rules for public adjusters in Pennsylvania. It raises the bond they must carry to $40,000, sets fee limits at 10% for catastrophe claims and 15% for other insurance claims, and bars fees before a claim is settled. It also adds rules on disclosures, referrals, licensing checks, and other limits on what adjusters and related businesses may do.
